subject: SLO deep dive: traffic envelope, concurrency, and live probe window
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Sara Malik <sara.malik@veridian.ai>, platform@veridian.ai
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 04 May 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — latency targets and streaming behavior

Hi Sara — thanks again for the productive call this morning. Quick recap and asks so we can scope the hosted SLO probe: 

Summary from our side:
- Veridian target: p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 380ms (end-to-end) for text generation calls.
- Burst concurrency today: ~120 concurrent streaming connections during peak workflows; sustained concurrency for inference is ~30 qps.
- Typical request size: 350 tokens average (prompt + response).

Immediate asks to land the probe:
1) Traffic envelope spreadsheet (per-minute arrival distribution for a 24h period) — helps set synthetic shaping.
2) Short sample traces (headers + timing breakdown) from current provider for p95/p99 windows — we only need anonymized timings.
3) Clarify streaming pattern: do you hold long-lived SSE/WebSocket connections with partial chunks, or re-open per request?
4) Confirm preferred live-demo window next week (we suggested Tue/Wed morning PT).

Attached: SLO_probe_template.xlsx (blank template to populate traffic envelope + concurrency slices).

Next steps: if you send the traffic envelope and samples today, Jordan can draft a probe-config and we can book a 60-minute shadow/demo to run the hosted probe against your staging endpoint.

Thanks —
Dylan
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0192

From: Sara Malik <sara.malik@veridian.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: platform@veridian.ai, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@veridian.com>
Date: Fri, 04 May 2028 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — latency targets and streaming behavior

Thanks Dylan — appreciate the concise list. Answers below and I attached a small CSV with a 24h sample and a handful of raw latency traces.

1) Traffic envelope: see column "per_minute_rps" in veridian_latency_samples.csv — peak minute hits ~1,900 requests, 15-minute rolling avg ~720 rps.
2) Current provider end-to-end observed: p95=140ms, p99=410ms (these are from last week's run on staging).
3) Streaming pattern: we use long-lived WebSocket connections and send token chunks as they arrive; clients keep a connection for the user session (avg connection lifetime ~6 minutes).
4) Live-demo: Tue 2028-05-09 09:00 PT works for our infra team.

Notes on constraints: some requests are fan-out (we call a reranker after the generator) which adds ~20–40ms additional latency in-path. We can mark that in the traces.

Attachment: veridian_latency_samples.csv (3MB - latency per minute + 20 row raw traces).

—Sara
Head of Platform Engineering | Veridian AI

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Malik <sara.malik@veridian.ai>
Date: Mon, 07 May 2028 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLO probe config draft and infra checklist

Dylan/Sara — I took a pass on the probe config using the CSV Sara sent. A few technical clarifications before we lock the run: 

- Traffic shaping: we'll replay per-minute RPS and also run a 5x burst test for 3 minutes to exercise tail behavior. Please confirm whether you want concurrent websocket sessions simulated as long-lived connections or ephemeral reconnects (we can do both).
- KV cache / prefix behavior: are mostly identical inputs or high variance? If identical prefixes are common we should enable prefix caching to reflect realistic gains.
- Observability hooks: we need a staging endpoint that exposes request-id headers so we can correlate traces; if not available we will inject a short-lived tracing proxy.

Proposed probe schedule (tentative):
- Tue 2028-05-09 08:15 PT — pre-check with Veridian infra (15m)
- Tue 2028-05-09 09:00 PT — hosted probe live run (60m)
- Tue 2028-05-09 11:00 PT — preliminary results and p95/p99 quick-check (30m)

Attached: streaming-checklist.md (internal checklist for websocket/session simulation).

If Sara confirms websocket semantics and agrees to the request-id header, I’ll finalize the probe config and share the exact canary routing rules (we'll run in shadow mode first).

-Jordan
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Sara Malik <sara.malik@veridian.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: platform@veridian.ai, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 May 2028 07:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLO probe config draft and infra checklist

Jordan — confirmed: production clients use long-lived WebSocket sessions. We can stand up a staging endpoint that preserves request-id header (X-Req-ID) for correlation. I've created a shared folder with traces and a staging access key: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XYZ-probe-plan

We're good for the Tue 09:00 PT window. I'll have one of our infra engineers on the call to help with any port/ACL adjustments.

Also flagged in our internal tracker: HS-1426 (tickets) for the tracing header — linking that for audit.

—Sara

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Sara Malik <sara.malik@veridian.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 May 2028 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLO deep dive: traffic envelope, concurrency, and live probe window

Great — thanks for the quick turnaround, Sara. Action items after this thread: 
- Jordan: finalize probe-config and shadow routing rules, push to our staging clusters by Mon 2028-05-15.
- Marissa: prepare a p95/p99 summary template so we can quickly fill and send post-run.
- Sara: share the staging access key and confirm infra engineer's name for the call.

We'll aim to surface an initial p95/p99 comparison vs. your current provider within 24h of the probe. If the tail looks promising, we'll talk dedicated capacity options and canary cutover policies next week.

Thanks — see you on Tue at 09:00 PT.

-Dylan
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
